title: U.S. House · Illinois's 14th District
area: Western Chicago suburbs and exurbs, including parts of Kane, Kendall, DuPage, and DeKalb counties.

context.text: Incumbent Lauren Underwood ran unopposed in the March 17, 2026 Democratic primary. James Marter defeated Gary Vician and write-in candidate Krystal Dorey in the Republican primary, 74.9% to 25.0% (Dorey 0.0%).

candidates.name: Lauren Underwood
candidates.ballotNote: Won the March 17, 2026 Democratic primary unopposed

summary.text: Lauren Underwood is the Democratic U.S. Representative for Illinois's 14th District and a registered nurse. Before her first election in 2018 she was a senior advisor at the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services and taught nursing students at Georgetown University. She is seeking a fifth term; her official biography lists her work on the House Appropriations Committee and her role as co-founder of the Black Maternal Health Caucus.

background.text: Born in Cuyahoga County, Ohio, and graduated from Neuqua Valley High School in Naperville, Illinois. According to Wikipedia, her family moved to Naperville when she was three and she graduated in 2004.
Earned a bachelor's degree from the University of Michigan in 2008 and a master's degree from Johns Hopkins University in 2009.

Is a registered nurse. She became a senior advisor at the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) in 2014 (per Wikipedia), where her official biography says she helped communities prepare for and respond to disasters, bioterror threats and public health emergencies and helped implement the Affordable Care Act.

Taught future nurse practitioners through Georgetown University's online master's program and worked with a Medicaid plan in Chicago on care quality and cost efficiency, according to her official biography.
Announced her candidacy in August 2017, won the 2018 Democratic primary, and defeated Republican incumbent Randy Hultgren in the November 2018 general election with 52.5% of the vote.

Was sworn in on January 3, 2019, and her official biography describes her as the first woman, first person of color and first millennial to represent the district. She was re-elected in 2022 (54.2%) and 2024 (55.1%).
Serves on the House Committee on Appropriations and is Co-Chair of the House Democratic Policy and Communications Committee.
Co-founded and co-chairs the Black Maternal Health Caucus. Her official biography describes her as a lifelong Girl Scout and says she lives in Naperville, Illinois.

priorities.text: Says her number one priority in Congress is ensuring access to high-quality, affordable health care and eliminating cost barriers to care.
Says she supports women's rights to the full range of reproductive health services, including access to safe, legal, and affordable abortion.
Says she believes the country must achieve a 100% clean energy economy by 2050.

positions.summary: Says she supports women's rights to the full range of reproductive health services, including access to safe, legal, and affordable abortion, and has voted for legislation to codify Roe v. Wade.
positions.quote: Lauren supports women’s rights to the full range of reproductive health services, without restrictions. This includes access to safe, legal, and affordable abortions.

positions.summary: Wrote the Health Care Affordability Act, signed into law as part of the American Rescue Plan and extended by the Inflation Reduction Act, which limits the cost of Affordable Care Act marketplace coverage to 8.5% or less of a household's income.
positions.quote: Lauren wrote the Health Care Affordability Act with her constituents top of mind. Signed into law as part of the American Rescue Plan, and later extended through the Inflation Reduction Act, the Health Care Affordability Act limits the cost of health care coverage for people who choose Marketplace plans to eight and a half percent or less of their income.

positions.summary: Says the country must achieve a 100% clean energy economy by 2050 and supported the Inflation Reduction Act as the largest climate investment in U.S. history.
positions.quote: Lauren believes we must achieve a 100% clean energy economy by 2050. That’s why she supported the Inflation Reduction Act, the single largest climate investment in U.S. history!

positions.summary: Supported House passage of the Bipartisan Background Checks Act and the Enhanced Background Checks Act to establish universal background checks for gun sales and close loopholes.
positions.quote: Lauren supported House passage of the Bipartisan Background Checks Act and the Enhanced Background Checks Act to establish universal background checks for all gun sales and close loopholes that make it easy for criminals to buy guns.

record.text: In the 119th Congress (2025-2026), serves on the House Committee on Appropriations (Agriculture, Rural Development, Food and Drug Administration and Related Agencies; Homeland Security).

candidates.name: James Marter
candidates.ballotNote: Won the March 17, 2026 Republican primary with 74.9% of the vote

summary.text: Jim Marter is the Republican nominee for Illinois's 14th Congressional District. He is a software consultant and business owner who, according to the Chicago Sun-Times, has been active in Kendall County Republican politics for about a decade. He was the party's 2024 nominee against Lauren Underwood, and won the 2026 Republican primary.

background.text: Graduated from Limestone Community High School and earned a B.S. in industrial management with a minor in computer science from Purdue University in 1984.
Received professional certification from the American Production and Inventory Control Society in 1995.
His career experience includes working as a software consultant, business owner and entrepreneur. In 2024 the Sun-Times described him as a self-employed software consultant from Oswego.

The Sun-Times reported that Marter said he has been engaged in local Republican politics for about a decade, including chairing the Kendall County Republican Party and serving as a precinct captain, and that he has served on Oswego's elected library board and was a 2024 delegate for Donald Trump.

The Sun-Times reported that since 2018 he had run three unsuccessful campaigns for the Republican nomination before winning it in 2024; in the June 28, 2022 primary he finished second to Scott Gryder.
Won the March 19, 2024 Republican primary with 79.0% and lost the November 2024 general election to Underwood, 55.1% to 44.9%.
Won the March 17, 2026 Republican primary with 74.9% of the vote over Gary Vician.

sources.title: U.S. Rep. Lauren Underwood defeats Republican Jim Marter in Illinois 14th Congressional District

researchNotes: James Marter has not completed the 2026 Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey and no campaign-website issue positions were located for him within the research budget for this race, so his priorities and positions are not documented here. Underwood's official house.gov priorities pages returned a 403 error when fetched; her campaign website was used instead. Marter's Ballotpedia page says he lives in Bartonville while the Chicago Sun-Times (2024) described him as from Oswego, so his residence is not stated in the biography; no campaign-website biography could be loaded (jimmarter.com returned 403).
